correctness.rationale: Every unit edge appears when at least one descendant survives; complete protection of leaf x gains exactly q^clade-size on each ancestor edge. Sorting ancestor clade sizes yields a componentwise dominance sufficient criterion for all q in (0,1). Recursive unordered binary root splitting covers all 24 shapes of orders 2..7 and supplies a dominating leaf for each; an independent labeled splitting generator checks all 11,465 labeled trees through 7 leaves. In the eight-tip witness all profiles are explicitly classified and the only competing score difference is q^3(q^2+q-1), with exactly one root. The independent 128-state survival enumeration verifies objective normalization for each witness taxon at two exact rational parameters.

evidence: Classical HED sum gives formula for each single protected leaf but does not imply which leaf maximizes it uniformly over an unknown risk without comparing all clade-size profiles.
Our explicit left-five/right-three witness has competing gains q+q²+q⁴+q⁵ and q+q²+q³, proving a strict crossover.
The all-seven guarantee follows from finite rooted shape dominance certificates; this quantified bound is absent from the inspected relevant papers.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A general algorithm returning the best leaf for each fixed parameter does not by itself state or establish the parameter-independent minimum size of a switching topology. General sensitivity examples with heterogeneous probabilities or nonunit edges are not the specific all-trees-before-eight theorem. An unknown stronger structural result remains a residual originality risk.

originality.rationale: Fixed-risk expected PD and HED scores are prior mathematics. Inspected exact full texts on expected PD, marginal HED, distributional PD, and robustness to uncertain extinction probabilities do not establish the new quantified statement: existence of a universally optimal taxon on every rooted full binary unit-edge tree through seven tips and a sharp eight-tip counterexample. The all-shape dominance certificate and exact crossover are not merely applications of a published minimum-order table. Originality remains provisional pending independent historical search.
residual_risks: A related resource-aware phylogenetic optimization paper (Pardi and Goldman 2007, DOI 10.1080/10635150701411279) was accessible only via abstract; a stronger unstated shape-classification theorem in that or other specialized literature has not been excluded.
Unindexed or differently described phylogenetic shape-dominance classifications may imply the same unit-edge cutoff; no literature search establishes absence of such works.

value.rationale: It resolves a natural complete small-size classification of whether a one-taxon equal-cost rescue priority can remain optimal when the common extinction risk is unknown. The minimal order eight, complete all-seven certificate, and explicit golden-ratio crossover are a structural limit of robust Noahs Ark conservation choice. It is not an arbitrary slice or a restatement of the known marginal score formula; it makes no empirical validation claims.
